messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV P1: multiple 5xx and TLS handshake failures to api.redwood.ai reported from EU & US edge POPs. Triggering page to oncall. Automatic failover attempted but saw increased connection resets.

alex-sre: seeing the same in our logs — spike of TLS handshake failures starting at ~1902345600. client error rates up 28%.

maya-eng: confirmed. curl from eu-west shows TLS handshake timeout: 
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/health
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (104.21.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* Handshake failed
* SSL: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
```

sam-platform: DNS queries show intermittent NXDOMAIN from our primary resolver clusters pointing at Cloudflare: 
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

emily-support: multiple customers reporting 502s and timeouts via support tickets (5 major accounts). Flagging for communications team.

aj-cloud: I've opened a ticket with Cloudflare support (ticket CF-11345). They've acknowledged a potential edge routing flap in EU-1 and US-C blocks. ETA unknown.

alex-sre: mitigation plan: 1) switch DNS to secondary authoritative in GCP DNS for api.redwood.ai as temporary A/AAAA record fallback, 2) enable direct origin routing on allowed IPs, 3) widen client TLS timeout to 10s on the LB, 4) enable non-proxied (DNS bypass) host header route for critical customers. Executing step 1 now.

maya-eng: copying runbook 'edge-dns-failover' steps. Doing DNS change now: 
```
# update in terraform is risky for speed, patch via gcloud
gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-primary
gcloud dns record-sets transaction add 34.102.154.12 --name="api.redwood.ai." --ttl=60 --type=A --zone=redwood-primary
gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=redwood-primary
```

alex-sre: added TTL 60, propagated to secondary. Running dig to verify.

maya-eng: dig shows new IPs from secondary DNS but some clients still hitting Cloudflare edge which returns 525/521. Need to reduce Cloudflare proxy TTL and disable Proxied for the zone for critical subdomain.

sam-platform: I'm preparing an automated play to rotate the CNAMEs off Cloudflare for the critical route and deploy a temporary ALLOW list of Cloudflare IPs for direct origin connections.

emily-support: drafting customer status update. Short note: "We're experiencing degraded API reachability from multiple cloud edge providers; we are failing over to alternate routing and working with the CDN vendor. We'll update in 30 minutes."

aj-cloud: Cloudflare replied: "We are investigating edge handshake timeouts in US-E & EU-W. Mitigation in progress. If you can route directly to origin IPs, that will bypass the affected POPs." Also asked for packet captures - leaving that for later.

alex-sre: performed route change to bypass Cloudflare proxy for /v1/customers/* for 4 impacted accounts (temporary). Monitoring.

maya-eng: logs show direct origin path responding normally for those accounts. Error rates for them down to baseline. :thumbsup:

oncall-handoff: paging next oncall @aj-cloud for 30m handoff. I'm leaving the incident channel and handing to aj-cloud to coordinate with Cloudflare and SRE. Key open items: 1) finalize DNS fallback for all regions, 2) confirm TLS certs ok for direct origins, 3) escalate to Cloudflare SE if not fixed in 20 minutes, 4) post customer communication.

aj-cloud: taking over. Reaching out to Cloudflare SE now, sent packet captures + SNI logs. Also enabling temporary healthcheck route that uses port 8443 to avoid proxy TLS termination.

sam-platform: added LB config to increase idle & handshake timeouts: 
```
# nginx upstream example
proxy_connect_timeout 10s;
proxy_read_timeout 60s;
proxy_send_timeout 60s;
```

alex-sre: starting synthetic checks from multiple regions to measure handshake success rate. Also enabling circuit breaker on our API gateway to fail fast for flows hitting edge timeouts.

maya-eng: quick note — for customers with strict IP allowlists, we've posted the temporary origin IPs to the support ticket and asked them to whitelist. Some are already responding.

emily-support: published status update to status.redwood.ai: "Investigating - API reachability degraded due to third-party CDN edge routing/TLS handshake errors. Mitigations in progress: DNS fallback, direct origin routing for impacted customers. Next update in 30m."

aj-cloud: Cloudflare support says they see high inter-POP routing churn and are applying a regional BGP dampening. They asked us to confirm origin certificate chain; confirmed OK. They estimate 15-25min to stabilize.

oncall-handoff: leaving notes for the next oncall: we've applied DNS fallback, partial bypass for critical customers, increased LB timeouts, and enabled circuit breaker. Monitor synthetic checks and error budget alarms. If stabilization doesn't happen by 1902347400 escalate to Cloudflare SE + Eng-Infra pager.

alex-sre: continuing to monitor. Will post when error rate back to baseline or if we need more aggressive steps (full zone unproxy).

emily-support: I'll send tailored customer comms to affected enterprise accounts with the temporary workaround steps and expected ETA.

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by alex-sre, aj-cloud. Labels: third-party:cdn, impact:partial, mitigation:dns-failover.

aj-cloud: Cloudflare reports partial recovery in EU-1; US should follow. Error rates trending down from 28% to 8% in the last 6 minutes. Continuing to watch for handshake errors.

oncall-handoff: handoff complete. Leaving channel, ping oncall if anything spikes.

alex-sre: final follow-up — after 50 minutes, metrics back to normal and Cloudflare confirms traffic normalized. Leaving the incident open for a postmortem. Please record timestamps and steps in the incident tracker (INC-2026-042).

emily-support: postmortem owner assigned: maya-eng. Communications closed with customers; no SLA credits requested so far.

maya-eng: will start timeline and root cause analysis. Initial hypothesis: Cloudflare inter-POP routing instability causing TLS handshake mismatches during proxy termination, amplified by low DNS TTL and some cached state.

incident-bot: Incident P1 resolved at 1902347400. Please file postmortem within 72h.
